metaDescription: Year-end office deep clean cost averages $0.18–$0.45/sq ft or $55–$95/hr for carpet extraction and December resets. Estimate rates in our cost calculator.
excerpt: Budget a December office reset with real US square-footage rates for hot-water carpet extraction, VCT scrub-and-recoat cycles, and post-party kitchenette recovery. Learn how scheduling during late-December vacant-suite windows eliminates overtime surcharges.
quickAnswer: A comprehensive year end office deep clean cost in the US averages $0.18 to $0.45 per square foot—or $55 to $95 per specialty labor hour—compared with $0.05 to $0.20 per sq ft for routine weekly cleaning ($90 to $135 minimum visit). A targeted December floor-only reset (hot-water carpet extraction or VCT scrub-and-recoat) typically runs $0.09 to $0.18 per sq ft per event (the equivalent of $0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month amortized quarterly), putting a full 5,000 sq ft suite reset at $1,000 to $2,250 and a 10,000 sq ft reset at $1,900 to $4,200.

blocks.text: Every December, commercial property managers face the same two operational realities: twelve months of embedded winter salt, coffee spills, and conference-room scuff marks peak right after the company holiday party—while unused Q4 facilities OPEX budget expires on December 31. Booking a **year-end holiday office deep clean** during the quiet final week of the year restores flooring warranties and resets indoor air quality before January staff return.

Unlike routine maintenance priced in our [national office cleaning cost guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/), a year-end reset shifts crews out of standard **$35 to $65 per hour** maintenance into **$55 to $95 per hour** specialty project work. Below is exact US pricing across suite sizes, floor materials, and holiday scheduling windows so you can lock a clean Q4 purchase order without emergency surcharges.
Year-End Office Deep Clean Cost Benchmarks by Square Footage

Standard nightly janitors sweep workstations at roughly **3,500 sq ft per labor hour** (2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr) using **$0.05 to $0.20 per sq ft** bracket pricing plus **$15 to $30 per restroom**. By contrast, a year-end deep reset slows production to **900 to 1,600 sq ft per hour** because technicians move perimeter chairs, run hot-water extractors, scrub ceramic grout, and detail overhead blinds and glass partitions.

If you only need restorative floor work rather than top-to-bottom wall and workstation detailing, standalone December carpet extraction or VCT recoating drops closer to **$0.09 to $0.18 per sq ft**—matching one quarterly cycle of our [amortized quarterly deep floor care guide](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/quarterly-deep-clean-amortized-monthly-cost/) (**$0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month**).

blocks.text: Notice that small suites under 2,500 sq ft often hit a **$250 to $450 specialty dispatch minimum** for truck-mounted extraction or auto-scrubber mobilization. Bundling your December floor work with your incumbent vendor—or scheduling a full suite reset alongside [one-time deep office cleaning benchmarks](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/one-time-deep-office-cleaning-cost-guide/)—prevents paying separate trip charges for carpet technicians and detail cleaners.
Itemized December Reset Modules: Carpet Extraction, VCT Recoat & High Dusting

Facility budgets stretch furthest when you price your December reset modularly instead of signing an open-ended time-and-materials ticket. Flooring type drives the largest variance: commercial carpet (**1.00x** baseline) requires hot-water extraction and pre-spraying along traffic lanes, while VCT/LVT (**1.04x**) needs neutral scrub-and-recoat or strip-and-wax, and ceramic tile with grout (**1.12x**) demands rotary brush agitation in restrooms and kitchenettes.

blocks.text: Using the December 24–January 1 Dark-Week Window to Cut Overtime

Timing is the easiest lever to trim 15% to 30% off your December deep clean quote. Most US offices experience minimal occupancy between **December 26 and December 30**—non-federal-holiday weekdays when commercial janitorial crews bill normal straight-time rates rather than the **1.5x to 2.0x holiday overtime premiums** triggered on Christmas Day or New Year's Day (see our [holiday office cleaning schedule pricing guide](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/holiday-office-cleaning-schedule-pricing/) for federal holiday clause rules).

Performing carpet extraction or VCT acrylic recoating in an unoccupied suite during those non-holiday workdays removes three major cost penalties at once: technicians do not wait on late-staying staff, chairs can be stacked cleanly across dry zones without blocking egress paths, and floors receive **6 to 12 hours of uninterrupted HVAC dry time**—preventing sticky soil attraction and footprint imprinting on fresh finish.

blocks.title: Use Expiring Q4 OPEX Budget Without Paying Rush Fees
blocks.text: Lock your year-end reset scope and purchase order before December 5 for execution on December 26–30. Waiting until the week of December 15 pushes crews into limited capacity and triggers 15% to 25% emergency dispatch premiums—or forces work into January under next year's budget.
Equipment, Slip-and-Fall Controls, and OSHA Compliance During Deep Resets

High-production year-end resets rely on commercial detailing tools rather than slow residential gear. After staff remove December window clings, garlands, and conference-room smudges, glass technicians clear full-height lobby sidelights and executive partitions quickly with the **Unger Professional 18-Inch Window Squeegee & Scrubber Kit**—pairing an anodized 18-in rubber blade and microfiber sleeve with an 8-ft telescopic pole for streak-free overhead reach without dragging step ladders across wet carpet.

Because multi-zone floor extraction and tile scrubbing leave damp thresholds across hallways simultaneously, crews prevent premises-liability slip claims by staging **Rubbermaid Commercial 25-Inch Multilingual Wet Floor A-Frame Sign (6-Pack)** sets at every elevator lobby, restroom corridor, and stairwell door; the 25-in tall yellow frames fold flat for compact cart transport and feature integrated carry handles. For high-density workstation rows, window blinds, and dual-monitor arms that collect static dust all year, detailers sweep rapidly with **Swiffer Dusters Heavy Duty 360 Commercial Starter + 24 Refills**, using a 3-ft extendable handle and 360-degree electrostatic fibers that capture fine particulate without scratching brushed aluminum or privacy glass.

blocks.title: Verify COI, OSHA HazCom, and Green Seal Standards for Project Crews
blocks.text: If you hire a specialty floor crew separate from your nightly vendor, require an active Certificate of Insurance ($1,000,000/$2,000,000 General Liability Additional Insured + Workers' Compensation), OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) Safety Data Sheets for carpet strippers and neutralizers, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) protocols for restroom restoration, and Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice low-VOC chemistry.
Scope Exclusions That Trigger Surprise Year-End Change Orders

Even detailed year-end deep clean bids exclude heavy building-engineering or specialty restoration work unless written into the Exhibit A scope. Audit your quote for these six common exclusions before issuing a PO:

items: **Heavy Furniture & Credenza Moving:** Crews will roll lightweight task chairs aside, but lifting loaded filing cabinets, modular desk pods, or server racks creates back-injury and IT liability; carpet is extracted around stationary footprints.

**Exterior Window Washing Above First-Floor Reach:** Interior glass detailing covers inside panes and reachable entry doors; exterior glazing above 8 to 10 feet requires rope-access or lift-certified window contractors.

**Inside-Refrigerator & Coffee Descaling Without Purge:** Food safety rules forbid cleaners from throwing away employee items; HR must mandate a pre-holiday fridge empty-out before the **$55 to $95/hr** appliance reset begins.
**HVAC Ceiling Diffusers & Plenum Ductwork:** High-reach exterior vent wiping is surface-only; internal duct cleaning falls to licensed mechanical/NADCA specialists.
**Task-Chair Fabric Extraction:** Upholstered office chairs typically bill separately at **$8 to $18 per chair** rather than inside per-square-foot carpet extraction pricing.

**Post-Party Biohazard & Red-Wine Dye Removal:** Standard extraction removes surface stains; bodily fluids (governed by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030) or dye-set spills on wool carpet add **$55 to $95 per specialty hour**.

blocks.text: 5-Step Year-End Deep Clean Procurement Timeline (November to December)

Follow this procurement sequence to lock competitive pricing and verify quality before your office reopens in January. Compare your incumbent's project quote against outside floor specialists in our [Quote Comparator](/compare-cleaning-quotes/).

items.name: Run a Late-November Daylight Walkthrough
items.text: Inspect carpet traffic lanes, VCT gloss levels, breakroom tile grout, and conference glass under daylight to choose between a floor-only reset ($0.09–$0.18/sq ft) or full reset ($0.18–$0.45/sq ft).

items.name: Request Bundled Pricing From Your Current Vendor First
items.text: Ask your recurring contractor for a bundled December add-on quote; because they already hold building keys, alarm codes, and an active COI on file, they often waive the $250–$450 mobilization fee.

items.name: Schedule Execution on Non-Holiday Dark-Week Days
items.text: Book carpet extraction and floor finishing between December 26 and December 30 so crews work straight-time hours in an empty suite without triggering 1.5x–2.0x federal holiday labor surcharges.

items.name: Confirm Building HVAC & Security Access Hours
items.text: Coordinate with building property management to keep ventilation running for 6 to 8 hours post-extraction so damp carpet dries completely without musty odors or humidity spikes.

items.name: Complete a Pre-Reopen Punch-List Inspection
items.text: Walk the suite on the final business morning before January return to verify dry floors, streak-free glass partitions, spotless appliances, and stacked consumables ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit restock).

faqs.q: How much does a year-end deep clean cost for a 5,000 sq ft office?
faqs.a: A full top-to-bottom year-end deep clean for a 5,000 sq ft US office averages $1,000 to $2,250 ($0.18 to $0.45 per sq ft, or roughly 10.5 to 23.0 specialty labor hours at $55 to $95/hr). If you only need hot-water carpet extraction and hard-floor machine scrubbing without high dusting or appliance detailing, expect $475 to $900 ($0.09 to $0.18/sq ft)—compared against $458 to $773 per routine visit on a 3x/week contract using 4.333 weeks per month billing.

faqs.q: Does a year-end deep clean cost extra during Christmas or New Year's week?
faqs.a: Work performed directly on observed federal holidays (December 25 or January 1) commonly triggers 1.5x to 2.0x overtime labor rates if you insist on holiday-day staffing. Scheduling your deep clean on regular non-holiday weekdays between December 26 and December 30 keeps rates at normal straight-time specialty pricing ($55–$95/hr) while taking advantage of an empty office.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to pay for an annual December floor reset or an amortized quarterly deep-floor plan?
faqs.a: A standalone December carpet and VCT reset costs $0.09 to $0.18 per sq ft once per year (plus a $250–$450 trip minimum for small suites), which is cheaper annually if foot traffic is light. High-traffic offices often add amortized quarterly deep floor care at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month inside their recurring contract, spreading four quarterly floor cycles across predictable monthly invoices.

faqs.q: What insurance and OSHA compliance documents should a year-end specialty cleaning crew provide?
faqs.a: Require an up-to-date Certificate of Insurance showing $1,000,000/$2,000,000 Commercial General Liability naming your company and landlord as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation for W-2 technicians, a janitorial bond, OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) Safety Data Sheets for floor strippers and spotters, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) compliance, and Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice low-VOC solutions.

faqs.q: What tasks are usually excluded from a standard year-end office deep clean quote?
faqs.a: Standard per-square-foot deep clean quotes normally exclude moving heavy desks or IT equipment, exterior windows above ground-floor pole reach, internal HVAC ductwork, shampooing fabric task chairs ($8–$18/chair extra), throwing away unmarked employee food in refrigerators without an HR purge rule, and emergency biohazard or dye-set spill remediation ($55–$95/hr).
